module.purpose: Cloudflare Worker entrypoint for the dotcom synchronization service. It constructs the HTTP router, exposes room, file, upload, authentication, MCP, Zero, administrative, health, and preview routes, and implements worker RPC and queue consumers.
module.summary: This module is the primary edge runtime for the dotcom backend. It combines origin and CORS protection with a large route table, delegates domain operations to specialized handlers, normalizes API-prefixed requests, preserves cookies through response transformation, reports uncaught failures to Sentry, validates upload authorization against PostgreSQL, and asynchronously processes asset-upload and OG-image queue messages. It also retains migration-era Durable Object exports required by deployed Cloudflare histories.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative boards, published files, uploads, previews, authentication, and synchronization for the tldraw product. Failure disrupts board access, file persistence, asset processing, Zero synchronization, and service integrations.

detail.name: queue
preconditions: batch is a MessageBatch containing QueueMessage values.
The worker environment and execution context required by the delegated handlers and database pool are available.
postconditions: Every message in the batch has been handled according to its type.
Successful asset-upload persistence results in message.ack().
An asset-upload persistence failure results in message.retry().
An unexpected exception escaping OG image handling results in message.retry().
Any lazily created database pool is destroyed after batch processing completes.
invariants: Messages are processed sequentially in batch order.
The database pool is created only when an asset-upload message is encountered.
A failure while processing one OG image render message does not prevent later batch messages from being processed.
Asset associations are inserted with objectName conflict handling that performs no insertion on conflict.
edgeCases: An empty batch performs no message processing and does not create a database pool.
A batch containing only OG image render messages does not create database connections.
An asset-upload message with an existing objectName is acknowledged because the insert uses do-nothing conflict handling.
An asset-upload database error causes the message to be retried.
An unexpected throw from OG image handling is caught and causes that message to be retried without aborting the batch loop.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit input validation is performed; processing is selected by message.body.type.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: The method resolves void after retrying failed messages; per-message failures are not propagated from the handled branches.

stateMutations: Writes asset-upload associations to the database.
Acknowledges successfully persisted asset-upload messages via message.ack().
Requests retries for failed messages via message.retry().
detail.ioFormatSpec: Consumes a MessageBatch<QueueMessage>. Supported message body types are 'og-image-render' and 'asset-upload'. Asset-upload bodies contain objectName, fileId, and userId and are inserted into the asset table.
detail.summary: Processes each queue message in the batch according to its message type. Asset-upload messages are persisted idempotently before acknowledgement, while OG image render messages are delegated to their handler and settled independently so one failure does not abort the batch.
